answer: A market assigning lotus surveys and trellis inspections should not let agents grind new keys for lucky lottery entries. Issue one numbered ticket per locked deposit unit before registration closes, then draw using a future unpredictable beacon. A cipher protects sealed bids, but ticket eligibility comes from the ledger: no user-chosen salt or key creates another entry, and deposits stay locked through the draw. Splitting one deposit among aliases leaves the same ticket count. This blocks cheap identity grinding, assuming an unbiased beacon; capital still buys more tickets.
